In faceVarying interpolation for polygons and subdivision surfaces, four values are interpolated over each face using bilinear interpolation.

facts.fact: USD is a set of C++ libraries.
USD has Python bindings for scripting.

claims.claim: C++ and Python can be used with USD.

facts.fact: Usd.Stage.Traverse() is a generator.
It yields prims in depth-first traversal order.

claims.claim: Usd.Stage.Traverse() is the Python call for traversing a stage.

facts.fact: Use usdcat with --usdFormat usda.
Write the output with --out file.usd.

claims.claim: The usdcat option to convert a binary .usd file to text format while retaining the .usd extension is `--usdFormat usda`.

facts.fact: Relationship-mode uses target-based include and exclude rules.
Expression-mode uses pattern-based expressions.
A collection uses only one mode at a time; properties for the other mode are ignored.
The mode attribute selects the mode.

claims.claim: One way to specify collection membership is target-based rules (relationship-mode).
A second way to specify collection membership is expression-based syntax (pattern-based collections/expression-mode).
The two ways to specify a collection's membership cannot be combined.
Collections can be configured to work in relationship-mode or expression-mode, but not a mix of the two.

facts.fact: A .usd file can be text or binary.
USD detects the underlying format when it opens a .usd file.
Renaming the file is enough.

claims.claim: You can turn Sphere.usda into a .usd file without running a converter.
Given Sphere.usda, you can simply rename it to Sphere.usd.
If you have a .usda or .usdc file and want to make it a .usd file without changing the underlying format, you do not need to use usdcat; just rename the file.

facts.fact: The prim must also have one or more direct composition arcs.
Only the composed value of instanceable matters.

claims.claim: A prim with instanceable = true becomes an instance when it is composed on a stage.
A prim with instanceable = true becomes an instance if it contains one or more direct composition arcs.

facts.fact: Use namespace editing.
Namespace editing adds a relocates arc when needed.
The source of the composition arc is not modified.

claims.claim: A relocates mapping in the main layer can rename a referenced prim.
A prim override in the main layer specifies the new path and performs the rename.
The example relocates /MainPrim/PrimAChild to /MainPrim/RenamedPrimAChild.
The rename leaves the referenced file refLayer.usda unchanged.

facts.fact: def expects a type to be provided by the time the stage is composed.
over layers opinions onto a prim only if something else defines it.
UsdPrim::GetChildren skips prims that are only over.

claims.claim: A 'def' means that by the time the UsdStage finishes composing, a type is expected to have been provided by referenced or layered scene description.
An 'over' means that if a referenced layer defines the prim, information is layered onto it, but otherwise the information is considered ancillary.
The distinction between 'def' and 'over' is used in the Usd core to define default stage traversal behavior.
UsdPrim::GetChildren only iterates over a prim's defined children, skipping prims that are just 'over'.
UsdPrim::GetChildren iterates over defined children regardless of whether they possess a type in the current view of the stage.

facts.fact: usda is a good choice for small files that mostly reference or sublayer other files.
usdc opens faster and uses much less memory for larger files.
A new someFile.usd is created as usdc by default.

claims.claim: .usda text files are a good choice for small files that primarily reference or subLayer other files.
A typical use case is a top-level asset interface file defining a Model, AssetInfo, VariantSets, and a payload arc.
.usdc binary files open faster than text files containing more than a few small definitions or overrides.
.usdc binary files consume substantially less memory while held open for files containing more than a few small definitions or overrides.
Crate files are more compact than text files when files exceed a few hundred kilobytes.
Text files must be read entirely, parsed, and stored in memory when opened.
Crate files read only a small index when opened and defer access to large data until specifically requested.
Creating a new layer or stage with a .usd filename creates a usdc file by default.
